decisions.rationale: Lead Rotom-Wash + Incineroar: Rotom-Wash OHKOs Pelipper with Volt Switch and walls Water attacks; Incineroar provides Fake Out tempo control and Intimidate to weaken physical Swift Swim sweepers. Back Serperior + Klefki: Serperior cleans Water-types with Contrary Leaf Storm after Pelipper falls; Klefki sets Light Clay dual screens to blunt rain-boosted attacks and spreads Prankster Thunder Wave to neutralise Swift Swim speed.
decisions.notebook: Matchup build carried from teambuilding. Plan: Same rain matchup we beat 2-0 in Week 1. Serperior is the hard counter to every Water-type, OHKOing Mega Swampert and threatening Basculegion/Primarina after one Contrary boost. Rotom-Wash walls Water attacks (Waterfall 28-47%, Wave Crash 52-77%), OHKOs Pelipper with Volt Switch, and burns physical Swift Swim sweepers. Incineroar provides Fake Out + Intimidate cycling to disrupt their tempo. Klefki sets dual screens behind Light Clay to blunt rain-boosted attacks; Thunder Wave neutralises Swift Swim speed. Mega Metagross deletes Whimsicott with Steel STAB and cleans with Bullet Punch. Corviknight offers Tailwind to match their speed tier and walls Whimsicott completely. Opponent may adapt with Mega Ampharos or Alakazam, but the core plan remains sound — remove Pelipper early, paralyse the Swift Swim sweepers, and let Serperior snowball. decisions.rationale: Bring Pelipper and Swampert to lead, setting up Drizzle immediately for Swift Swim Speed and activating Damp Rock. Back them with Basculegion and Whimsicott for strong sweeping and speed control.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Pelipper + Swampert, back: Basculegion + Whimsicott. Rain core establishes immediate offensive pressure against Incineroar and Metagross.

decisions.rationale: Volt Switch OHKOs Pelipper (131-260%) removing their rain setter; Fake Out flinches Swampert to prevent any attack or Mega Evolution this turn. Even if Pelipper Protects, Swampert is still neutralised. If both Protect we reset cleanly. Worst case Pelipper outspeeds for Tailwind before dying — still a winning trade removing Drizzle permanently.

Serperior is the hard counter to Mega Swampert: Leaf Storm is a guaranteed OHKO from 90% (145-252%). Swampert's Ice Punch does only 40-58% and Earthquake a mere 15-21% (Grass resists Ground). Even if Swampert outspeeds the narrow speed tie (Serperior 181 vs Swampert 180-244), Serperior survives any single hit and KOs back. The opponent must hard-read the switch and double-target with Ice Punch plus a strong special Fairy move to have a chance at KOing Serperior before it moves — an unlikely prediction when Waterfall into Incineroar is the obvious play. After the KO, Serperior sits at +2 SpA from Contrary, threatening Basculegion (85-155% Leaf Storm) and snowballing out of control. Incineroar stays in to preserve momentum; its Focus Sash guarantees it lives any single hit, enabling Parting Shot or Flare Blitz next turn.

decisions.rationale: Serperior Leaf Storm into Swampert-Mega: guaranteed OHKO if it doesn't Protect, and Contrary gives +2 SpA either way. Incineroar Protect avoids the likely double-target from Swampert-Mega Earthquake + Basculegion Wave Crash, which would otherwise KO through Focus Sash (EQ breaks Sash, Wave Crash finishes). This preserves both mons and removes or forces Protect from their Swift Swim sweeper.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Leaf Storm OHKOs Basculegion through the speed tie while boosting Serperior to +4 SpA via Contrary. Parting Shot debuffs Whimsicott (-1 SpA/Atk) and pivots Incineroar into Klefki, preserving the Focus Sash Incineroar for later. Whimsicott's Prankster Tailwind or Encore both resolve first, but either outcome is manageable: Encore locks Serperior into the Leaf Storm it's already using, and Tailwind gives them speed control but leaves them with a solo debuffed Whimsicott against Serperior + Klefki. Klefki can set Prankster Light Screen next turn to neuter Moonblast. Switch target after Parting Shot: Klefki.

Incineroar's Focus Sash intact, Parting Shot pivoting to Klefki. Klefki and Rotom-Wash still fresh in back. Opponent's unrevealed Primarina and Ampharos not brought.

decisions.rationale: Serperior stays in at +4 SpA with Contrary snowball; forfeiting a dominant 2v1 is absurd. Incineroar at 1% dies to any Moonblast, so switch to Klefki, which resists Moonblast (Steel/Fairy), can Thunder Wave to neutralize Whimsicott's Tailwind speed, and sets Light Screen to further blunt Moonblast damage. Rotom-Wash is also viable but offers no Fairy resist and burn is low value vs a special attacker.

Next turn, +6 Leaf Storm OHKOs even through resistance regardless of paralysis RNG.

Klefki's Foul Play also KOs, providing insurance against the 10% miss chance. Whimsicott cannot OHKO Serperior with Moonblast (20-32%), so the game is won regardless of Speed order or Whimsicott's move.

Primarina and Ampharos were left in team preview. For game 2, expect opponent to bring Primarina (Fairy-type, Hyper Voice) or Ampharos-Mega (Mold Breaker Dragon Pulse) to handle Serperior. reflections.summary: Serperior's Contrary Leaf Storm snowballed after early KOs on Pelipper and Swampert, and the opponent's Encore only locked it into further boosts, leading to a quick sweep.
reflections.adjustment: Expect Primarina or Ampharos-Mega to counter Serperior. Consider leading Klefki to set screens and slow them with Thunder Wave, and preserve Serperior for late-game after removing Fairy/Dragon threats.

reflections.summary: The opponent's Serperior capitalized on Contrary and Life Orb with unchecked Leaf Storm boosts while Incineroar and Klefki controlled the field, snowballing out of control after neutralizing the Swift Swim and rain offense early.
reflections.adjustment: Prioritize immediate offensive pressure or taunt on Serperior to prevent Contrary Leaf Storm setup, and ensure speed control is established safely against Fake Out.
